answer.evidence: The crystal cluster (rows 1-14) is decor sitting on the pedestal. The pedestal top is a thin gray slab at rows 13-15. It is 12 wide at rows 12-14 and narrows to 10 at row 15, with a light edge line at row 14 and a shadow at row 15. That reads as a 2-3 row rim or band. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small crystal on a grey stone pedestal, much smaller and simpler than the references (stall, well, hedge). Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line, not a tint of the adjacent material. This matches the sticker look, unlike the tinted outlines on the hedge, stall and well. The pedestal reads as a flat grey block with only about 2-3 steps and little stone texture or per-stone shading. The crystal has a few facets of light blue and white, but they are limited and fairly shallow. The 9 visible tones per tile are comparable to the hedge, but they come from a tiny footprint with a neutral outline, and the stall (17) and well (20) are clearly richer. Near-flat coverage of 14% is similar to the stall, but the pedestal body still shows flat areas. Overall the piece is cleaner and flatter than the Beodeul standard, with shallow shading and a neutral outline.
